title: Gradient Descent Visualizer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Data Science
description: Take gradient descent steps on a contour map of a cost function, read the gradient and the next position at each step, and change the learning rate to see slow progress, zigzag, and divergence.

educational.topic: Gradient descent and the learning rate
learningObjectives: Students will be able to apply the gradient descent update rule to calculate the next parameter values and predict how the learning rate changes the path to the minimum.

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Step-through of an algorithm with every intermediate value shown, followed by parameter exploration
keyQuestions: Why do the steps get shorter near the minimum even though the learning rate has not changed?
Why does the elongated valley diverge at a learning rate that works on the simple bowl?
What does the gradient point toward, and why does the update subtract it?
On the two valleys surface, what decides which minimum the path reaches?
commonMisconceptions: The gradient points at the minimum (it points in the direction of steepest increase at the current position; the opposite direction is downhill, which is not always straight toward the minimum).
A larger learning rate always reaches the minimum sooner (past a threshold the steps overshoot and the cost grows).
The step size is the learning rate (the step is the learning rate times the gradient, so it shrinks as the surface flattens).
Gradient descent always finds the lowest point (on a surface with more than one valley it stops in whichever valley its path enters).
assessmentOpportunities: Given $J = w_1^2 + w_2^2$, a starting point, and a learning rate, students compute two gradient descent steps by hand and explain what would happen if the learning rate were 1.2.
